mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (below 2.0%) compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS (as of t-1mo) is below 2.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 4.0% signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 4.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 250) and rising interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%) signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 250 and FEDFUNDS > 2.0%, or the Rank IC for the interaction term over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 250), the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, reducing equity valuations and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 250, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
